title: This shit can be so frustrating... but I love it
author: 710cartman
selftext:
I would get hate for this in a lot of subs, but:

I've always wanted to do game design. When I was a little kid, I told my parents I wanted to learn Japanese so I could help make Nintendo games (yeah, I know that's dumb asf in hindsight but I was like, 5 years old).

But life happens and I never learned to really code. When I was younger I got into some script writing and made some shitty HTML pages, but never "real" coding. I also went through a Photoshop phase, but never "real" graphics design. 

And now, I can be a lead game designer. Maybe my game never makes a penny and no one plays it but me while iterating. And for sure, sometimes it's frustrating in many ways.

But damn if it isn't everything I thought it would be. I really do love it.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
It can be frustrating but moreso when you code yourself. I was a game designer in the mid 2000s and even with large teams it can get frustrating when your code won't work right.

It's funny and almost jarring to NOT be looking at lines of code all day. Instead that's replaced with a robot with the temperament of a toddler.

"NO god damn it, why are you adding the NPCs from stage 1 to stage 2??"
"Well you said add NPCs so I just added them all. Also here's an extra lifebar, and I've gone ahead and removed your debug tool."

comments.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
comments.body: ive been directing a game, i love seeing it come nicely to be more and more playable, i already added a good amount of content and am now trying to polish the rest of the functions before i keep going, its a fun little hobby to do in my free time
